references.text: Moses' prayer in Exodus 33:18-20 to see the Lord's glory, and God's response that no one can see His face and live, stands in direct contrast to Jesus' claim in John 14:9 that one can see the Father by seeing Him.
God's self-revelation to Moses in Exodus 34:6-7, where He proclaims His name and character, is the same revelation of the Father that Jesus claims to be in John 14:9.
John 1:18 confirms the theological premise in John 14:9 by stating that no one has ever seen God, but the only Son, who is in the bosom of the Father, has made Him known.
Hebrews 1:3 describes Jesus as 'the radiance of God's glory and the exact imprint of his nature,' a direct parallel to Jesus' words in John 14:9 that whoever has seen Him has seen the Father.
